title: The elevator smoking case · the appeal court's reasoning
speaker: Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court, Henan (appeal)

groups.label: Issue 1: is Yang Fan liable in ordinary tort?
Issue 2: does the first instance's fairness liability apply?
Issue 3: Yang Fan did not appeal; may the appeal court change the judgment?

nodes.label: The first-instance judgment is set aside and Tian Jiuju's claim dismissed: Yang Fan bears no tort liability
Civil Procedure Law Art. 170(1)(2): the ground on which an appeal court changes a judgment
Yang Fan is liable in ordinary tort (fault liability)
Tort Liability Law Art. 6(1): a person who infringes another's civil rights through fault bears tort liability
The dissuasion was improper and went beyond what was necessary
There is a legal causal link between the dissuasion and Duan Xiaoli's death
Yang Fan acted intentionally or negligently
Yang Fan's dissuasion was rational and calm and stayed within what was necessary: it was proper
The dissuasion and the death are only one after the other in time; there is no legal causal link
Yang Fan dissuaded a smoker as a citizen's duty to society, and had no intent to harm Duan Xiaoli
The dissuasion of smoking cannot in itself cause Duan Xiaoli's death
Yang Fan could not foresee Duan Xiaoli's death, and was not careless or negligent
Lift camera (clock 09:24): Duan Xiaoli was smoking in the lift; after Yang Fan came in the two began to talk
The three videos have pictures and no sound; the two only talked, with no pulling and no physical clash
Throughout, Yang Fan was relatively calm and restrained; Duan Xiaoli was agitated, and more so as time went on
There is no evidence that Yang Fan shouted at Duan Xiaoli or did anything else improper
Yang Fan and Duan Xiaoli were in contact for less than five minutes
120 was called at 09:31 and the paramedics reached the patient at 09:37
Yang Fan had not known Duan Xiaoli, and did not know of his medical history or his heart bypass operation
Once he knew, Yang Fan promptly used his professional skill to help Duan Xiaoli
Yang Fan should pay Tian Jiuju 15,000 yuan on the fairness principle (what the first instance did)
Tort Liability Law Art. 24: where neither victim nor actor was at fault, the loss may be shared as the facts require
There is a legal causal link between the act and the harm, and neither side was at fault
There is no legal causal link between the dissuasion and the death, so the precondition of Art. 24 is not met
In applying Art. 24 and the fairness principle the first instance applied the law wrongly
The first instance, because Duan Xiaoli died suddenly after the quarrel with Yang Fan, ordered Yang Fan to pay Tian Jiuju 15,000 yuan
The appeal court should change the first-instance judgment
Civil Procedure Interpretation Art. 323: an appeal is tried on the grounds of appeal, unless the judgment breaks a legal prohibition or harms the State, the public interest or another's rights
Zhengzhou's rules: smoking is banned in lifts and other public places, and citizens may stop it
The basic principles and purpose of civil law: protect the environment, uphold the public interest and public order and good morals, promote core socialist values
The first-instance judgment harms the public interest (the exception to trying an appeal only on its grounds)
Yang Fan's dissuasion was lawful and proper: a conscious act to uphold public order and the public interest
Making a citizen who dissuaded properly share the loss would dampen citizens' will to defend the public interest, harm it, and run against the purpose of civil law
Yang Fan did not appeal after the first-instance judgment
